questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy design, RBAC scoping, and CI integration for a high-sensitivity platform.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- RBAC bindings (RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding)
- Namespace-scoped allowlists and auditing in CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-namespace allowlist)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RbacWhitelist
metadata:
  name: rbac-whitelist-prod
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [\"rbac.authorization.k8s.io\"]
      kinds: [\"RoleBinding\", \"ClusterRoleBinding\"]
  parameters:
    namespaceAllowlists:
      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
      staging: [\"view\"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this with CI/CD and simulate violations?
- How would you handle dynamic/temporary permissions without conflicting with the allowlist?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question validates hands-on policy-as-code experience with Istio across multi-cloud environments, assessing understanding of security posture, observability, and CI/CD integration. It confirms the candidate's ability to implement zero-trust networking principles in service mesh architectures.

## Key Concepts

- **Istio AuthorizationPolicy with SPIFFE IDs**: Cryptographically verified identities for service-to-service authentication using the Security Working Group's Architecture for Inter-Network Secure Communication (SPIFFE) standard
- **Mesh-wide sidecar injection**: Ensuring all pods have Envoy proxies for mutual TLS (mTLS) and policy enforcement
- **Default-deny egress**: Implementing network isolation by blocking all outbound traffic by default, explicitly allowing only required destinations
- **OpenTelemetry trace propagation**: Maintaining distributed tracing context across service boundaries for observability

## Evaluation Focus

Candidates should demonstrate:
- Familiarity with Istio CRDs (AuthorizationPolicy, Sidecar, PeerAuthentication)
- Understanding of SPIFFE identity format (spiffe://<trust_domain>/ns/<namespace>/sa/<service_account>)
- Knowledge of OpenTelemetry context propagation headers (b3, w3c TraceContext)
- Ability to write CI validation scripts using kubectl, istioctl, or custom validators

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical enforcement of runtime posture using admission controls and network egress in a multi-tenant data platform. Combines Gatekeeper and Kyverno with real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate with REGO to require envoy-proxy sidecar in confidential pods
- Kyverno policy enforcing non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem and sidecar presence
- NetworkPolicy egress allowlist for data exfiltration guardrails
- CI test plan with manifest validation; runtime validation via in-cluster policy, egress monitoring

## Code Example
```rego
package k8svalidation

deny["envoy-proxy sidecar required"] {
  input.review.object.metadata.labels["data-tier"] == "confidential"
  not has_sidecar(input.review.object.spec.containers, "envoy-proxy")
}

has_sidecar(containers, name) {
  containers[i].name == name
}
```

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: confidential-pod-security
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-envoy-sidecar
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              data-tier: confidential
    validate:
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: envoy-proxy
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to translate security requirements into a enforceable policy and CI flow for a multi-tenant cluster. It also evaluates practical policy testing across PRs.

## Key Concepts

- Kyverno ClusterPolicy for container securityContext checks
- Kubernetes pod/spec validation in Deployments/StatefulSets
- CI gate integration with PR workflows
- Test manifests to verify both compliant and non-compliant cases

## Code Example

```javascript
// Kyverno policy (as YAML in practice)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-privileged-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-secctx
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job"]
    validate:
      message: "Container must drop ALL capabilities, run as non-root, and readOnly rootfs"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop:
                    - ALL
```

## Why This Is Asked

This checks practical CI gating for namespace discipline and Helm workflow. It exercises a concrete validation using YAML parsing and shows how to tie environment mapping to PR gates.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes namespaces
- Helm charts values.yaml
- YAML parsing with yq
- GitHub Actions gate
- Environment-specific deployments

## Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ENV="${ENV:-dev}"
for f in manifests/**/*.yaml; do
  NS=$(yq e '.metadata.namespace // ""' "$f")
  if [[ -z "$NS" || "$NS" != "$ENV" ]]; then
    echo "Namespace mismatch: $f -> '$NS' (expected '$ENV')"
    exit 1
  fi
done
```

```yaml
# failing manifest (namespace: default)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
  namespace: default
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
```

```yaml
# passing manifest (namespace: prod)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
  namespace: prod
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:1.0.0
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in policy-as-code across multi-cloud, multi-tenant ML infrastructure. It combines security hardening (image signing, secret management), resource governance (GPU quotas, container limits), network segmentation (default-deny policies), and operational reliability (canary deployments with SLO validation)—all critical for enterprise-grade ML platforms.

## Key Concepts

- **Policy Engines**: Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper provide declarative, Kubernetes-native admission control
- **Image Signing**: Cosign ensures container image integrity and provenance verification
- **Secret Management**: ExternalSecret/SecretStore enables secure, dynamic secret injection from external stores
- **Resource Quotas**: ResourceQuota and LimitRange enforce compute, memory, and GPU allocation per tenant
- **Network Policies**: Namespace-scoped default-deny with per-tenant allow rules implements zero-trust networking
- **Canary/SLO Integration**: Prometheus metrics validate deployment health before traffic shifting
- **CI Integration**: Automated policy testing and manifest validation ensure consistent enforcement

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy: require Cosign-signed images from approved registries
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: check-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*.gcr.io/tenant-*/**"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "*@company.com"
```
